newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Hospital Pantai issue off; plans bonus.
newsitem.headline: Hospital Pantai issue off; plans bonus.

text.p: Malaysia's Hospital Pantai Bhd (HPB) said it was calling off an issue of four million shares at a price of 10.00 ringgit each and was instead planning a four-for-one bonus issue.

But it will go ahead with the planned transfer of its listing to the main board from the second board of the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange, the national Bernama news agency quoted the company's merchant bank as saying.

The four-for-one bonus issues of up to 376 million ringgit would be capitalised from the company's share premium account, its second merchant banker said in a statement. The total bonus would depend on the conversion of outstanding loan stock.
Apart from increasing the liquidity in its shares, the bonus issue would complement the transfer of the company to the main board of KLSE.
Hospital Pantai's entire issued and paid-up capital together with five-year five percent Irredeemable Convertible Unsecured Loan Stocks will move to the main board.
Hospital Pantai will also not proceed with the proposed acquisition of Healthcare Holdings (Cayman) Limited and Alpha Healthcare Limited from Berjaya Group Equity (Cayman) Limited.
However, it will continue with the acquisition of Merjiwa Medical Associates Sdn Bhd for 8.5 million ringgit and the radiotherapy business of Radio-Med Sdn Bhd for 2.39 million.
The proposed acquisitions, originally to be financed with funds from the proposed issue, will now be financed by internally-generated funds, the statement said.
Its first merchant banker said noted that Hospital Pantai will have a gross cash of 686 million ringgit from the sale of 60.182 million shares in Singapore-based Parkway Holdings Limited.
It said the proposed expansion of the hospital on four pieces of leasehold land have yet to be completed.
Trading in Hospital Pantai shares were suspended on Tuesday at the company's request. It was last traded at 28.75 ringgit per share.
